content: The provided text is a detailed pharmacological interaction profile for the drug etravirine, focusing on its effects on various other drugs through hepatic and intestinal enzyme metabolism, particularly involving the cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzyme system. 1. Etravirine and Ranolazine: Etravirine reduces the plasma levels or efficacy of ranolazine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated, and alternative therapies should be considered. 2. Etravirine and Regorafenib: Etravirine decreases regorafenib levels while increasing the exposure of its active metabolite M-5 through CYP3A4 induction. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Etravirine and Repaglinide: Etravirine lowers the levels or effects of repaglinide by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. 4. Etravirine and Repotrectinib: Etravirine decreases repotrectinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism but increases its levels through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Avoidance or alternative drugs are recommended. 5. Etravirine and Ribociclib: Etravirine reduces ribociclib levels through CYP3A4 metabolism, while ribociclib increases etravirine levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 6. Etravirine and Rifabutin: Rifabutin decreases etravirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drugs are recommended unless specific dose adjustments are made. 7. Etravirine and Rifampin: Rifampin significantly reduces etravirine levels by inducing CYP3A4, CYP2C19, and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 8. Etravirine and Rifapentine: Rifapentine decreases etravirine levels through CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 induction. This combination is contraindicated. 9. Etravirine and Rifaximin: Etravirine increases rifaximin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Etravirine and Rilpivirine: Etravirine reduces rilpivirine levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated, as rilpivirine should not be used with NNRTIs. 11. Etravirine and Rimegepant: Etravirine decreases rimegepant levels via CYP3A4 metabolism but increases its levels through P-glycoprotein inhibition. Avoidance or alternative drugs are recommended. 12. Etravirine and Riociguat: Etravirine reduces riociguat levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 13. Etravirine and Ripretinib: Etravirine decreases ripretinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drugs are recommended. 14. Etravirine and Ritonavir: Ritonavir increases etravirine levels through CYP3A4 inhibition, while etravirine reduces ritonavir levels. This interaction is preparation-dependent, and some combinations are contraindicated. 15. Etravirine and Roflumilast: Etravirine reduces roflumilast levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 16. Etravirine and Rolapitant: Etravirine decreases rolapitant levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drugs are recommended. 17. Etravirine and Saxagliptin: Etravirine decreases saxagliptin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 21. Etravirine and Sildenafil: Etravirine reduces sildenafil levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Etravirine and Simvastatin: Etravirine reduces simvastatin levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drugs are recommended. 26.
